name: Gearbox
text: Deploy the AMD MI325X cluster running Llama 4 70B as EXCAVA’s primary engine. It’s the fastest open-weight model we can run in-house right now, cutting inference latency by 30% over the current stack. The trade-off is higher power draw and cooling load, but the net gain in throughput outweighs the cost.

name: Torque
text: Locking into AMD MI325X risks a single-vendor death spiral—if AMD shifts pricing, drops support, or exits the AI chip market, EXCAVA’s primary engine becomes a stranded asset. A safer play is to dual-run Llama 4 70B on MI325X *and* a secondary stack (e.g., NVIDIA H100 with vLLM) for 6 months; if the AMD cluster’s 30% latency cut holds without stability issues, migrate fully—otherwise, the fallback keeps us unblocked. Settle it with a 30-day bake-off measuring throughput, power cost per token, and failure rates under load.

name: Gearbox
text:
Dual-run Llama 4 70B on both the AMD MI325X and an NVIDIA H100 with vLLM for six months. This approach mitigates the risk of dependency on a single vendor and maintains flexibility, allowing us to adjust quickly to market shifts. The trade-off is increased complexity in management and potential costs associated with running two systems, but this strategy enhances stability and future-proofs EXCAVA's architecture. This decision prioritizes reliability while still striving for significant power gains.

name: Torque
text: Dual-running MI325X and H100 doubles the operational overhead—two stacks to patch, monitor, and scale—without solving the core risk: if Llama 4 70B degrades or AMD/NVIDIA shifts pricing, we’re still locked to a single model family. A better hedge is to split the load: run Llama 4 70B on MI325X for latency-critical tasks, but offload 20% of queries to a secondary model (e.g., Qwen3 235B) on a third-party API for 6 months; if the secondary model’s quality or cost drops below 95% of the primary, we kill the experiment. Settle it by measuring end-to-end latency, cost per token, and win-rate drift across both stacks for 30 days—no vendor wins if the secondary underperforms.
